digest.headline: US stock indexes reached new record highs driven by major technology shares as central bank officials discussed future rate paths.

lede.b: US stock indexes reached new record highs as big technology shares drove the broader market advance. US Treasury yields, which are a way for governments to borrow money by paying investors interest over time, stalled during this equity session. Federal Reserve official Daly noted that the necessity for further rate hikes depends entirely on future shocks. Bond market pricing adjusted as investors digested these central bank remarks. PIMCO senior advisors described current Treasury yields as screaming good value.

A PIMCO senior advisor described current Treasury yields as screaming good value.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: US stocks reach new highs as tech shares climb

stories.t: Stock Indexes Reach New Highs
stories.b: The S&P 500 index reached a brand new record high. An index is a group of different company shares measured together to track a market. Big tech companies helped push the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite to their peaks. The Nasdaq Composite is another collection of mostly technology stocks. Big tech companies helped drive these indexes up.
stories.i: The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite scaled new peaks. Big technology shares drove the broader market advance. These indexes reached record highs during the session. Large technology companies powered the upward move.
stories.a: Major equity benchmarks advanced to fresh record highs. Mega-cap technology constituents catalyzed the upside momentum in both the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite. Broad market participation concentrated heavily in these tech leaders. Price action reflected continued strength in the primary large-cap growth segments.

stories.t: Treasury Yields and Rate Perspectives
stories.b: US Treasury yields stalled during the trading day. Yields are the return an investor gets on government debt, which is like a fixed-interest loan made to the state. A PIMCO senior advisor called US Treasury yields screaming good value. Meanwhile, Fed official Daly discussed whether more interest rate hikes will be needed. Hikes are increases in the central bank's benchmark borrowing cost.
stories.i: US Treasury yields stalled alongside the record equity session. A PIMCO senior advisor described current Treasury yields as screaming good value. Federal Reserve official Daly noted that the necessity for further rate hikes depends entirely on future shocks. Bond market pricing adjusted as investors digested these central bank remarks.
stories.a: US Treasury yields stalled as broader risk assets rallied. PIMCO senior personnel characterized current yield levels as compelling value propositions. Federal Reserve commentary from Daly emphasized that additional monetary tightening remains contingent on exogenous shocks. Duration positioning responded directly to shifting perceptions of the terminal rate.

politics.b: Government officials and central bankers discussed the economy.
politics.i: Federal Reserve policymakers evaluated macroeconomic shocks.
politics.a: Central bank officials calibrated policy reaction functions against potential macroeconomic shocks.

timeline: Fed official Daly spoke about rate hikes and potential shocks.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: London stocks rise on oil and yields

stories.t: London equities rise as oil prices drop
stories.b: The FTSE 100 index gained 0.46%. This index tracks the 100 biggest companies listed in London. Lower oil prices helped push the index up. Defence shares fell at the same time.
stories.i: The FTSE 100 closed 0.46% higher. Softer oil prices provided a lift to broader equities. Defence shares lagged behind the wider market advance.
stories.a: The FTSE 100 index advanced 0.46%. Energy input costs receded as crude prices softened, supporting index constituents while defence equities underperformed.

stories.t: Informa advances following Clarion deal
stories.b: Informa shares rose today. The company gained ground after an agreement involving Clarion. This helped the FTSE 100 extend its gains.
stories.i: Informa shares climbed following a transaction involving Clarion. The move added momentum to the broader FTSE 100 advance.
stories.a: Informa shares rallied on corporate activity concerning Clarion. The gain contributed to the FTSE 100 extension.

politics.b: A central bank official warned about stubborn price rises. The pound reacted to these comments.
politics.i: A Bank of England hawk warned that inflation remains embedded. The GBP/USD currency pair caught bids following the remarks.
politics.a: A Bank of England hawk highlighted entrenched price pressures. Sterling appreciated against the dollar as market participants processed the monetary policy warnings.

timeline: The FTSE 100 closes 0.46% higher amid easing gilt yields

Germany.label: Germany
Germany.sub: German stocks climb to two-week high as oil prices drop

stories.t: DAX Index Rises
stories.b: The main German stock market index, called the DAX, went up by 0.82% at the close of trade. Shares reached nearly a two-week high. Falling oil prices and lower yields helped push stocks upward. A yield is the return an investor gets on a bond, which is like a loan made to a government or company. Oil fell below $100 a barrel.
stories.i: The DAX closed up 0.82% to reach a near two-week high. Declining oil prices and easing gilts boosted equity valuations across the session. Crude dropped below $100 a barrel.
stories.a: German equities advanced as the DAX gained 0.82% to touch a two-week high. Sovereign debt yields compressed alongside falling crude prices, which slipped beneath $100 per barrel.

stories.t: Factory Orders Decline
stories.b: German factory orders slumped on the same day stocks rose. The DAX index still climbed by 0.82% by the end of the trading day. Lower oil prices helped offset the weak factory data. Oil traded at under $100 a barrel.
stories.i: German factory orders slumped while equities advanced. The DAX gained 0.82% at the close. Falling crude prices below $100 a barrel provided a tailwind for the index despite the weak manufacturing figures.
stories.a: Factory orders dropped sharply even as the DAX added 0.82% at the close. Energy price relief counterbalanced the weak industrial prints. Brent and WTI benchmarks retreated below $100 per barrel.

politics.b: Police arrested a former German spy chief. Authorities suspect him of attempted treason.
politics.i: Law enforcement detained a former German intelligence chief. Authorities brought preliminary charges of attempted treason.
politics.a: State prosecutors apprehended a former intelligence chief. Authorities filed allegations regarding attempted treason.

timeline: The DAX closes up 0.82% as oil prices fall below $100 a barrel.
A former German spy chief is arrested on suspicion of attempted treason.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Startale launches Japan digital bond in yen stablecoin

stories.t: Startale launches digital bond paid in stablecoin
stories.b: Startale Japan launched the first digital bond in the country paid in a yen stablecoin. A digital bond is a debt instrument tracked on a computer network instead of on paper. The project pays interest and principal in JPYSC. This means investors receive their returns using digital currency.
stories.i: Startale Japan issued the country's first digital bond settled in a yen stablecoin. The instrument distributes both interest and principal payments in JPYSC tokens. This digital issuance bypasses traditional clearing infrastructure.
stories.a: Startale Japan deployed the domestic market's inaugural digital bond denominated and settled in a yen stablecoin. The structure distributes coupon and principal obligations entirely in JPYSC. This issuance tests on-chain settlement efficiency for fixed-income assets.

politics.b: Xi Jinping left Japan uncertain about a China summit at APEC. The leaders discussed diplomatic meetings.
politics.i: Xi left Japan uncertain regarding a bilateral summit with China at APEC. The diplomatic schedule remains undecided.
politics.a: Xi left the Japanese administration uncertain regarding a bilateral summit at APEC. Diplomatic channels continue to navigate scheduling friction.

timeline: Startale Japan launched the country's first digital bond paid in a yen stablecoin.

China.label: China
China.sub: DeepSeek funding rounds and regional trade milestones

stories.t: DeepSeek Considers Up To $15 Billion Funding Round
stories.b: DeepSeek is an artificial intelligence company. It creates computer systems that can reason and write. DeepSeek is raising money from backers like Tencent and CATL. Backers give money to a company in exchange for a piece of the business. DeepSeek is considering a funding round of up to $15 billion.
stories.i: DeepSeek is considering doubling its latest funding round to reach up to $15 billion. Tencent and CATL are among the backers participating in this capital raise. The artificial intelligence firm previously contemplated a $12 billion raise.
stories.a: DeepSeek weighs scaling its current funding vehicle to as much as $15 billion, doubling prior targets. Strategic backers Tencent and CATL anchor the syndicate. This follows initial discussions around a $12 billion raise.

stories.t: China-Asean Trade Reaches 4.34 Trillion Yuan in First Half
stories.b: Trade is the buying and selling of goods between countries. China and the countries in Asean traded a huge amount of goods together. The total value reached 4.34 trillion yuan in the first half of the year. A yuan is the money used in China.
stories.i: China-Asean trade volume hit 4.34 trillion yuan during the first half of the year. This figure measures the total cross-border exchange of goods and services. Asean comprises a bloc of Southeast Asian nations trading actively with the Chinese economy.
stories.a: Bilateral commerce between China and Asean prints at 4.34 trillion yuan for the first half. This metric captures aggregate import and export flows across the regional trade bloc. The print underscores the depth of supply chain integration within the partnership.

politics.b: Xi Jinping has not yet confirmed if he will attend a summit with Japan at APEC. Leaders meet at summits to talk about politics and trade between nations.
politics.i: Xi Jinping left Japanese officials uncertain regarding his attendance at a bilateral summit during the APEC gathering. Diplomatic channels continue to monitor the scheduling of top-level talks.
politics.a: Xi's participation in a bilateral summit with Japan on the sidelines of APEC remains unconfirmed. Diplomatic signaling around the event introduces friction into regional multilateral engagements.

timeline: DeepSeek considers raising its funding round up to $15 billion
China-Asean trade hits 4.34 trillion yuan in the first half of the year

India.label: India
India.sub: RBI auctions, NBFC credit data, and State Government Securities

stories.t: Reserve Bank of India Schedules Variable Rate Reverse Repo Auction
stories.b: Central banks use actions like reverse repo auctions to manage the money circulating in the banking system. The Reserve Bank of India announced a overnight variable rate reverse repo auction for October 7, 2026. This auction has a notified amount of 3,00,000 crore rupees and a single day tenor. Banks can place bids during a window on October 7, and the reversal takes place on October 8, 2026. Operational guidelines govern the exact execution of this monetary tool.
stories.i: The central bank announced an overnight variable rate reverse repo auction under the liquidity adjustment facility for October 7, 2026. This operation targets systemic liquidity by absorbing 3,00,000 crore rupees for a single day tenor. Counterparties submit bids during a morning window, with funds reversing on October 8, 2026. Such liquidity management tools help the authority steer short-term interest rates toward the target policy rate.
stories.a: The liquidity adjustment facility operation absorbs surplus base money via a 3,00,000 crore rupee variable rate reverse repo tender with a 1-day tenor maturing on October 8, 2026. This overnight absorption mechanism addresses transient banking system cash imbalances before the upcoming monetary policy decision. The pricing discovered in this variable rate auction reveals the marginal cost of short-term funds among participating commercial institutions.

stories.t: Non-Banking Financial Companies Record Credit Expansion in August
stories.b: Lending by non-banking financial companies and housing finance companies grew significantly. Data for August 2026 shows a credit growth rate of 15.8 per cent on a year-on-year basis. This is higher than the 10.0 per cent growth rate recorded a year ago. The Reserve Bank of India collects these sectoral figures from major institutions.
stories.i: Sectoral deployment data released by the central bank indicates robust credit expansion across non-banking financial companies and housing finance companies. Credit extended by these lenders grew by 15.8 per cent year-on-year in August 2026. This figure marks an acceleration from the 10.0 per cent growth rate observed during the same period a year earlier. The statistics derive from returns filed by major non-bank lenders.
stories.a: Aggregate credit deployment by non-banking financial companies and housing finance companies accelerated to 15.8 per cent year-on-year in August 2026, up from 10.0 per cent a year prior. This persistent credit velocity underscores robust domestic demand for non-bank financing channels despite tightening monetary conditions. The data reflects underlying asset growth trends across major institutional portfolios sampled by the regulator.

stories.t: State Governments Raise Funds Through Security Auctions
stories.b: State governments borrow money by issuing debt securities to the market. The Reserve Bank of India published the full results of a state government securities auction held on October 6, 2026. Andhra Pradesh issued securities maturing in 2035 and 2042 with notified amounts of 1,000 crore rupees each. Delhi re-issued securities maturing in 2033 and 2041 with notified amounts of 500 crore rupees each.
stories.i: State governments executed debt issuance through a scheduled auction of state government securities on October 6, 2026. Andhra Pradesh raised funds via re-issues of its 2035 and 2042 paper, each carrying a notified amount of 1,000 crore rupees. Delhi secured financing through re-issues of its 2033 and 2041 debt, each set at 500 crore rupees. The auctions distribute sub-sovereign risk across institutional portfolios at established coupon rates.
stories.a: Sub-sovereign debt issuance concluded with Andhra Pradesh placing 1,000 crore rupees across its 7.46% 2035 re-issued paper and 1,000 crore rupees in its 7.79% 2042 paper. Simultaneously, Delhi cleared 500 crore rupees in its 7.31% 2033 re-issued state government securities alongside another 500 crore rupees in its 2041 tranche. These re-issues expand existing benchmark lines, enhancing secondary market liquidity for sub-sovereign debt.

politics.b: Equities rose ahead of the central bank policy decision. The BSE Sensex gained 685 points to close 0.95 percent higher. The Nifty index reclaimed the 22,700 level.
politics.i: Domestic equity benchmarks advanced as investors positioned themselves ahead of the impending central bank policy announcement. The BSE Sensex closed 0.95 per cent higher, driven by a gain of 685 points. The Nifty index crossed the 22,700 threshold amid a broader market recovery.
politics.a: Equities rallied into the policy announcement window, with the BSE Sensex advancing 0.95 per cent and the Nifty reclaiming the 22,700 handle. Market breadth reflected broad participation in the recovery pullback, supported by easing crude oil prices. This price action occurred alongside foreign exchange intervention where authorities sold dollars to counter currency depreciation.

timeline: State Government Securities auction results published

Brazil.label: Brazil
Brazil.sub: Brazilian markets rally following election results

stories.t: Brazilian assets surge after presidential election
stories.b: The main Brazilian stock index, called the Ibovespa, went up sharply. This happened because investors felt very positive after the presidential election results came out. When an index goes up, it means the average value of a group of important companies has risen. Petrobras, a huge state-backed energy company, saw its shares jump by 11.5%. Other major firms like Vale, SABESP, and Ambev also climbed.
stories.i: The Ibovespa index extended its election-driven rally as political optimism lifted domestic equities. Petrobras shares jumped 11.5% following the vote. Three other corporate giants, namely Vale, SABESP, and Ambev, also registered strong gains. Capital flows returned to the region as sentiment shifted after the presidential ballot.
stories.a: The Ibovespa extended its bullish momentum following the presidential election outcome, catalysing aggressive inflows into domestic equities. Petrobras surged 11.5%, pacing a broader large-cap rerating that included Vale, SABESP, and Ambev. The positive political backdrop prompted foreign institutional capital to return to Brazilian assets, compressing risk premia across the index.

stories.t: Petrobras secures major gas contracts and expands operations
stories.b: Petrobras carried its strong second-quarter profit surge directly into October. The energy giant locked in a 22-year liquefied natural gas contract with Cheniere Energy. It also reached a separate deal with Sempra for liquefied natural gas. At the same time, Petrobras pushed ahead with an offshore gas exploration campaign in Colombia.
stories.i: Petrobras maintained its second-quarter profit momentum into October alongside new commercial agreements. Cheniere Energy secured a 22-year liquefied natural gas contract with the Brazilian producer. Sempra announced a separate liquefied natural gas deal with Petrobras, prompting Scotiabank to set an USD 83.00 target for Sempra stock. Meanwhile, Petrobras expanded its offshore gas footprint through a campaign in Colombia.
stories.a: Petrobras leveraged its robust second-quarter earnings surge into Q4 catalysts by executing multi-decade supply agreements. Cheniere Energy finalised a 22-year liquefied natural gas off-take contract with the state-backed producer, matching a separate arrangement struck with Sempra. Concurrently, operational breadth increased via an offshore exploration campaign in Colombia.

stories.t: Brazilian real strengthens against US dollar following vote
stories.b: The Brazilian real, which is the official currency used in Brazil, strengthened in value against the United States dollar. TD Securities noted that the country's political backdrop heavily favors gains for the local currency. Analyst Brooks stated that capital is returning to Brazil, which could drive the real up even higher. Coffee prices also rallied due to the strong real combined with risks from the El Niño weather pattern.
stories.i: The Brazilian real traded down against the US dollar following election-driven optimism. TD Securities highlighted that the domestic political backdrop favours further gains for the currency against the greenback. Brooks noted that returning capital could accelerate the currency rally. Meanwhile, coffee prices advanced due to the stronger real and ongoing El Niño risks.
stories.a: The Brazilian real appreciated against the US dollar as post-election sentiment bolstered foreign exchange demand. TD Securities cited a constructive political backdrop supporting structural gains for the currency against the greenback. Brooks projected extended appreciation as cross-border capital repatriation gains traction. Concurrently, coffee futures rallied on the dual tailwinds of currency strength and El Niño meteorological risks.

politics.b: Brazil held a presidential election that changed market sentiment. Investors reacted with optimism to the voting outcome. This political shift encouraged capital to flow back into the country.
politics.i: The recent presidential election sparked widespread market optimism across domestic assets. Election results altered the political backdrop, driving a surge in equities and currency strength. Capital inflows responded directly to the political outcome.
politics.a: The presidential election results reset the domestic risk matrix, precipitating a sharp compression in asset risk premia. Optimism surrounding the ballot outcome catalyzed immediate equity rallies and currency appreciation. Macroeconomic sentiment pivoted as institutional capital initiated repatriation flows.

timeline: Petrobras and Cheniere Energy agree to a 22-year LNG contract.

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia.sub: Aramco awards major oil field contracts amid supply warnings

stories.t: Aramco Awards Major Infrastructure Deals for Safaniya and Marjan
stories.b: A company called Tecnimont and a partner named CCC won a project worth over $900m from Saudi Aramco for the Safaniya field. Saudi Aramco also gave a contract to KBR for work on the Marjan oil field. These deals involve building onshore facilities and upgrading offshore areas.
stories.i: Saudi Aramco awarded a project valued above $900m for the Safaniya field onshore facilities to Tecnimont and CCC. The state oil producer additionally contracted KBR for upgrade work on the Marjan offshore field. Both engineering agreements focus on expanding and maintaining key oil field capacity.
stories.a: Tecnimont and CCC secured a contract exceeding $900m for the Safaniya field onshore facilities from Saudi Aramco. Concurrently, KBR received an award for offshore upgrades at the Marjan field. These capital expenditure awards underline ongoing upstream development despite tight regional supply metrics.

stories.t: Aramco Chief Warns of Thin Global Oil Reserves and Strait Bottlenecks
stories.b: The head of Saudi Aramco said global oil supplies are dangerously thin. He warned that market pressure will continue until the Strait of Hormuz reopens. Rebuilding world oil reserves could take up to two years.
stories.i: The chief executive of Saudi Aramco described global oil stockpiles as scarily thin. Market pressures will persist until the Strait of Hormuz reopens according to reports. Rebuilding global inventories may require up to two years.
stories.a: The chief executive of Saudi Aramco characterised global oil stockpiles as critically thin. Persistent market tightness will remain until the Strait of Hormuz reopens and normalization occurs. Rebuilding depleted global reserves will require a timeline extending up to two years.

politics.b: OPEC held meetings with the second and third biggest oil consumers. Meanwhile, a Houthi attack caused smoke near a facility at Khurais.
politics.i: OPEC held discussions with the second and third largest oil consuming nations. Separately, a Houthi strike targeted an installation at Khurais.
politics.a: OPEC convened formal meetings with the second and third largest global oil consumers. Concurrently, a Houthi attack generated smoke near the Khurais facility.

timeline: Tecnimont and CCC secure a $900m+ Safaniya contract from Saudi Aramco.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Naira movements, borrowing spikes, and Dangote refinery plans

stories.t: Naira Trades at N1,331.5 per Dollar
stories.b: The official foreign exchange market values the Nigerian naira at N1,331.5 against the US dollar. Currencies are bought and sold at rates that change every day based on supply and demand. This official rate is tracked through a specific platform called the NFEM window. The exchange rate helps determine how much imported goods cost within the country.
stories.i: The Nigerian naira closed at N1,331.5 per dollar in the official foreign exchange market. Market participants executed trades through the CBN NFEM window. Official exchange rates fluctuate daily based on commercial bank matching and central bank guidelines. Currency depreciation directly affects the local purchasing power for foreign goods.
stories.a: The official NFEM window settled the naira at N1,331.5 per dollar, reflecting ongoing official market depreciation. Interbank liquidity conditions and central bank intervention parameters dictate these daily fixing levels. Market participants monitor the spread between this official rate and parallel market quotes to gauge true foreign exchange scarcity.

stories.t: Nigerians Increase Borrowing Amid Rising Costs
stories.b: More people in Nigeria are taking out loans because things cost too much. When everyday items get expensive faster than wages grow, families run out of money. Borrowing money lets people pay for basics like food and transport. This trend shows how hard it is for households to pay for daily life right now.
stories.i: Mounting cost pressures across the economy force Nigerian consumers to rely more heavily on debt. Households face severe purchasing power constraints as everyday expenses outpace income growth. Commercial lenders report higher demand for short-term credit facilities to cover basic living requirements. This credit reliance underscores the financial strain on domestic consumers.
stories.a: Persistent cost-of-living pressures drive an uptick in household credit utilization across the financial sector. Consumers absorb rising expenses by tapping short-term debt instruments, indicating constrained real disposable incomes. This credit expansion carries implications for non-performing loan ratios if household cash flows deteriorate further.

stories.t: Dangote Refinery Targets Retail Investors
stories.b: The CEO of Nigeria's Dangote refinery wants to attract more everyday investors than a major stock offering by Aramco. Aramco is a massive oil company from Saudi Arabia that sold shares to the public. Retail investors are normal people who buy small amounts of stocks rather than giant investment funds. The refinery aims to make everyday citizens owners of the business.
stories.i: Dangote refinery targets a larger retail investor base than the massive Aramco initial public offering, according to its chief executive. Retail participation involves individual everyday buyers acquiring shares rather than institutional funds. Company leadership aims for broad public ownership of the massive refining asset. This strategy differentiates the upcoming equity distribution from traditional energy listings.
stories.a: Management at the Dangote refinery projects retail investor participation to surpass the historic Aramco IPO metric. This ambition targets decentralized equity distribution rather than reliance on institutional bookbuilders. Capturing retail capital requires overcoming domestic liquidity hurdles and designing accessible subscription channels for individual shareholders.

politics.b: The Central Bank of Nigeria lowered interest rates to help businesses produce more goods. Lower rates make borrowing cheaper for companies that build and manufacture things. Government leaders hope this will boost local production and economic activity. No political parties or elections were mentioned in these updates.
politics.i: The Central Bank of Nigeria implemented a rate cut specifically designed to stimulate productive activities across the economy. Monetary authorities lowered borrowing costs to encourage industrial expansion and commercial investment. Officials intend for cheaper credit to drive output in manufacturing and agriculture. The policy adjustments operate independently of electoral cycles.
politics.a: Monetary policy easing by the Central Bank of Nigeria aims to channel liquidity into productive sectors. Lower policy rates reduce the cost of capital for industrial operators and agricultural producers. This intervention attempts to counter supply-side cost pressures through lower financing expenses rather than direct fiscal subsidies.

timeline: The Central Bank of Nigeria defends its rate cut as a measure to stimulate productive activities.
The official NFEM window records the naira closing at N1,331.5 per dollar.
Dangote refinery chief executive states the facility aims to draw more retail investors than the Aramco IPO.

Australia.label: Australia
Australia.sub: Property shares drive index gains as currency recovers

stories.t: Property Stocks Lift Index
stories.b: The S&P/ ASX 200 index is an official list that tracks the value of the 200 biggest companies trading on the share market in Australia. This group of shares went up by 0.57 percent at the close. Property stocks led the bounce in the market. The S&P/ ASX 200 closed 0.57 percent higher.
stories.i: The S&P/ ASX 200 finished higher by 0.57 percent. Property stocks drove the gains in the session. The S&P/ ASX 200 closed 0.57 percent higher after the rally.
stories.a: The S&P/ ASX 200 closed up 0.57 percent following a sector rotation into real estate equities. Property stocks underpinned the broader index advance. The S&P/ ASX 200 ended the session 0.57 percent higher.

stories.t: Australian Dollar Rises Against US Currency
stories.b: The Australian Dollar went up against the US dollar. Currency traders expect interest rates in America to stay the same in October. A weaker US currency helped the Australian Dollar advance.
stories.i: The Australian Dollar advanced against a weaker US dollar. Markets priced in an interest rate hold by the Federal Reserve for October. The Australian Dollar recovered as US yields remained a factor for traders.
stories.a: The Australian currency appreciated against the greenback as rate futures priced in a Federal Reserve hold for October. US yield dynamics continued to influence cross-border capital flows. The Australian Dollar advanced on a weaker US Dollar.

politics.b: No political news was reported in the market updates today.
politics.i: No government or policy updates featured in the financial reports.
politics.a: Electoral and legislative developments were absent from the trading sessions.

timeline: Property stocks rebound and lift the S&P/ ASX 200 index by 0.57 percent
The Australian Dollar advances against the US dollar as markets price in a Fed hold
